description: Is it safe to update? Right before or after a game patch, reads the game's version, the script extender build, its Address Library file and every script extender plugin DLL (game folder and Mod Organizer 2), applies the script extender's own published compatibility rules, and says which plugins would be refused. Covers Skyrim Special Edition and Anniversary Edition (SKSE) and Fallout 4 (F4SE). For GTA V (Legacy or Enhanced) it reads the game's version, Script Hook V's DLL and its log from the last launch, and says whether Script Hook V supports this version and whether a waiting Steam update would stop it. Verdict is go / check / wait, with a reason per plugin and a note on whether each rule is the script extender's own or inferred. Local and read-only — no network, nothing written or kept. Pass targetVersion (e.g. 1.7.104 for Skyrim, 1.11.240 for Fallout 4, 1.0.1158.16 for GTA V) to check a patch that isn't installed yet. A GO means every check that can be run from files passed; it can't promise the game runs. Use when the user asks "is it safe to update", "Steam updated Skyrim and now it won't start", "did SKSE break", "did F4SE break", "Script Hook V says unknown game version", "my GTA mods stopped working after the update", or "which plugins will break after the patch".

gameId.description: Canonical game ID: 'skyrimspecialedition', 'fallout4', 'gta5' (GTA V Legacy) or 'gta5enhanced' (GTA V Enhanced). Leave it out to check the game whose executable is in gamePath, or else the first one installed in a Steam library (Skyrim Special Edition first, GTA V last); the answer names any other one it found.

gamePath.description: The install folder (the one holding SkyrimSE.exe, Fallout4.exe, GTA5.exe or GTA5_Enhanced.exe), when ModWrench can't find the game on its own — a GOG copy, GTA V from the Rockstar Games Launcher or Epic, or a Steam library in an unusual place.

logPath.description: Path to skse64.log (or f4se.log) if it isn't in the usual Documents/My Games folder, or to ScriptHookV.log if it isn't in the GTA V folder. The script extender's own log from the last launch is cross-checked against the predictions.

mo2InstancePath.description: Mod Organizer 2 instance folder, for a portable instance that doesn't live where MO2 normally keeps them. Without it, MO2 is read only when it looks like the active manager.

profileName.description: MO2 profile name. Default: the instance's active profile.

targetVersion.description: A game version to check instead of the installed one, like '1.7.104' (Skyrim), '1.11.240' (Fallout 4) or '1.0.1158.16' (GTA V). Use it before updating; the number is in the Steam patch notes or on the SKSE, F4SE or Script Hook V site.
